items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: >> [(prose)] Don Redmon, who was one of the greatest arrangers, in my estimation, and one of the greatest rehearsers of a band -- [(prose)] he was Fletcher's first alto saxophonist and arranger...

ctx.x: ear. Jimmy Harrison was a great trombonist. He knew nothing about chords or anything. He just played the way he felt in his heart, but he wanted to learn how -- what notes were in certain chords, and Hawk would tell him, you know. And other guys would ask -- the trumpet player -- Henry Red Allen, incidentally, was in on this session too. And he was one of the few trumpet players that I know of that could run a diminished chord against a major and make it sound good. He'd invert it on the end and come back to the…
Don Redmon, who was one of the greatest arrangers, in my estimation, and one of the greatest rehearsers of a band --

he was Fletcher's first alto saxophonist and arranger, one of the very first ones with Fletcher. Even before Fletcher had started to really get out into the arranging field, Don first started Fletcher's book -- Don Redmond. And of course the guitarist, Charlie Dixon, from over in New Jersey was another guy that picked up arranging and turned out to be terrific.
